questions.question: An hour into a session, Claude seems to have forgotten details from early on. You want to see what is using up its working space. What do you run?
questions.explanation: /context shows how full the context window is and what each category, such as tools, memory files and messages, takes up. /compact and /clear change the conversation instead of showing it, and /config opens settings.

questions.question: You're halfway through a refactor and the context window is nearly full. You want to keep going on the same task. What should you do?
options: Run /compact and say what to keep
Paste the full log so Claude has everything
questions.answer: Run /compact and say what to keep
questions.explanation: /compact replaces the conversation with a summary, so you keep the decisions and progress and free the space. /clear throws the conversation away, and pasting more text fills the window further.

questions.question: Early in a session you told Claude "always use tabs in this project". After a compaction, it starts using spaces. What is the most reliable fix?
options: Repeat the rule after every compaction
questions.explanation: Chat messages survive compaction only as part of a summary, and details can be lost. CLAUDE.md is reloaded from disk after compaction, so a rule there comes back word for word.

questions.question: You asked Claude to read every file in a large folder "just in case". What is the cost?
options: The files take up context window space
Claude can edit those files without asking
The files are added to CLAUDE.md
questions.answer: The files take up context window space
questions.explanation: Everything Claude reads stays in the context window until it's compacted or cleared, leaving less room for the work you actually need. Reading a file doesn't change permissions or CLAUDE.md.

questions.question: You've finished a bug fix and want to start an unrelated feature. Which command fits best?
questions.explanation: /clear starts a fresh conversation, which suits unrelated work. /compact keeps a summary of the old task you no longer need, and /context only shows usage.
